Sample.evidence_source: [page/6/Text/5] Eight participants (under the age of 26 years) were recruited via youth networks, in response to an invitation to ". . . participate in some research on queer male youth, suicide, and the coming-out process."

Country.evidence_source: [page/7/Text/3] Sam (19 years), Ken (23 years), Tim (20 years) and Victor (19 years) identified as New Zealand European/Pakeha. Zac (19 years) identified as South African Indian/New Zealander. Carl (18 years) and Leon (20 years) identified themselves as Maori/New Zealander, and Henry (21 years) identified himself as Maori/Scottish and Chinese.

Population.evidence_source: [page/6/Text/5] Interested participants were asked in a pre-interview discussion whether they had ever attempted suicide before. Persons who indicated that they had attempted suicide were then asked if they felt psychologically and emotionally able to discuss the event without causing themselves undue distress and pain. None of the volunteers decided to withdraw. After four attempters and four non-attempters volunteered to participate, sampling finished. Equal numbers of attempters and non-attempters were interviewed so as to provide a range of experiences for analysis.

Type.evidence_source: [page/6/Text/5] Qualitative data were collected from in-depth 1- to 2-hour interviews.
